subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should deferred context-engine maintenance use this new opt-in compaction configuration key and core-owned timeout/fence lifecycle, rather than retaining the current unbounded behavior or adopting a different shared timeout contract?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and preserves existing behavior by default, but selecting a new durable configuration surface and the permanent ownership boundary for abandoned plugin work is a product and compatibility decision, not a mechanical review repair.

options.title: Sponsor the opt-in timeout model
options.body: Accept the new disabled-by-default setting and core-owned fence/checkpoint as the supported recovery path for wedged background maintenance.

options.title: Use an existing timeout policy
options.body: Ask for a narrowly redesigned patch that uses an established compaction or runtime timeout contract instead of adding a distinct configuration key.

options.title: Defer the feature direction
options.body: Keep the underlying bug open and pause this PR until maintainers define the permanent timeout and plugin-lifecycle contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the opt-in timeout model
recommendation.body: Accept the new disabled-by-default setting and core-owned fence/checkpoint as the supported recovery path for wedged background maintenance.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current implementation and can answer implementation tradeoffs, although a current-main feature owner should make the final product decision.
